title: Redwood discovery - model selection - Harbor Systems
summary: Discovery call to understand Harbor Systems' model selection requirements across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Key needs: long-context (20k+ tokens) for document workflows, strong multilingual capabilities (EN, ES, FR, ZH), tool-calling for internal retrieval and external APIs, enterprise security (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and predictable latency for SLAs. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and open-model options (LlamaX-style, Mistral, Falcon variants). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send Dedicated pricing + SOC2 pack, run a short benchmark on Harbor's 8k and 20k sample documents, and schedule a technical deep-dive with infra/security.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO - Harbor), Ravi Menon (ML Eng - Harbor), Dana Liu (Security), Tom Fletcher (Product)

[00:00] Sara (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call then we'll jump in, i'm sara kim, aefrom redwood, and miguel's our se today.
[00:19] Lena (Harbor): hey lena park here, raji's on mute, oh sorry ravi, ravi and dana and tom are with me.
[00:28] Miguel (Redwood SE): hi all, miguel ortega. excited to dig into the model selection needs.
[00:34] Ravi (Harbor): ravi, ml eng. we own the retrieval pipeline and runtimes.
[00:40] Dana (Harbor Security): dana, security/compliance.

[00:44] Sara: objective for today — understand your workloads (context length, multilingual, tool-calls), current infra, and any security constraints. then we can recommend hosted/dedicated/private and model families. sound good?
[00:53] Lena: yeah, high level yes. we have a doc-heavy product, customer support transcripts, legal contracts — need long context.
[01:03] Tom: also multilingual — about 30% spanish/french, some chinese.

[01:12] Miguel: got it. quick qual — are you prototyping on cloud infra today? what does your stack look like?
[01:19] Ravi: currently we use GCP for training; inference is mixed. small workloads on OpenAI endpoints, but we're running our own hosted models on GKE for specific tasks. we're seeing latency spikes and costs are creeping up.
[01:32] Sara: typical. any hard reqs on data residency or VPC?
[01:37] Dana: yes — for enterprise customers in EU we need data residency and audit trails, and our legal team wants KMS integration and SOC2 evidence. SSO must be SAML.
[01:47] Sara: noted. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem; Dedicated gives reserved capacity with KMS and private networking options.

[02:00] Miguel: diving into models — what context lengths are you aiming for? you said doc-heavy. can you quantify?
[02:06] Lena: our immediate need is 8k to 12k for support+attachments, but roadmap is 20k+ for full contract parsing and long conversation history.
[02:15] Ravi: ideally we'd like to test 8k and 20k scenarios. how do open models handle that vs managed?

[02:22] Miguel: short answer — some open models have longer context variants (recompilers or models trained with extended contexts) but latency and memory requirements grow. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache management and kernel selection to optimize larger contexts; we auto-select kernels and can advise on quantization profiles to keep costs down.
[02:39] Ravi: any specific models you recommend for 20k context? i've heard about Mistral/Longformer variants and some LlamaX forks.
[02:47] Miguel: yes — Mistral XXL-like long-context variants are promising, also Falcon with extended context, and newer Llama-derived checkpoints that support 32k contexts. the caveat is throughput — the higher context you hit, latency per request goes up and batching behavior changes.

[03:05] Tom: on multilingual — do these open models do well for ES/FR/ZH? we need decent domain adaptation for support tickets.
[03:12] Miguel: many open models are primarily english-optimized, but there are multilingual checkpoints and instruction-finetuned variants that do reasonable work in ES/FR. Chinese is trickier, often needs model variants trained on zh corpora. Redwood can host different model families and route requests based on language detection to the best variant.
[03:29] Lena: so we'd want routing by language; that makes sense. any maintenance burden?
[03:34] Sara: with Hosted you get a curated catalog and Redwood manages model updates and infra. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more control for model pinning. Private puts the control plane with you and you manage upgrades — common for strict compliance.

[03:52] Dana: on compliance — SOC2 is a must, and audit logs for model inputs/outputs. can you provide redacted logs? we can't keep raw pii longer than 30 days.
[04:02] Sara: yes, Redwood supports configurable retention and audit logs; SOC2 pack available. we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and support SAML SSO and RBAC.
[04:13] Dana: and encryption at rest for model weights?
[04:18] Miguel: for Private deployments you control key management and storage. in Dedicated/Hosted, we use envelope encryption with KMS and can offer bring-your-own-key for certain tiers.

[04:30] Ravi: what about tool-calling / function calling? we need to call our internal retrieval API and a billing API during responses.
[04:36] Miguel: Redwood supports streaming + structured output and function/tool calling primitives. we can surface a tool-call hook to call your retrieval service; plus run chained calls with deterministic fallbacks if a tool fails.
[04:48] Tom: is that supported across model families or only specific ones?
[04:51] Miguel: most modern transformer families support returning structured tokens; we build wrappers to parse tool-call intents. function-calling reliability can vary by checkpoint; we recommend testing with the target model.

[05:05] Sara: any cost constraints? you mentioned OpenAI usage before — are you trying to reduce that spend?
[05:10] Ravi: yeah, our monthly inference bill for OpenAI is around $25k and it's spikey. if we can push high-volume stuff to hosted/dedicated open models at lower unit cost that helps. but we need similar latency and accuracy.
[05:22] Miguel: typical pattern — low-latency/high-quality queries stay on managed models (or high-tier dedicated), while bulk retrieval and summarization can run on optimized quantized variants in Dedicated. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and batching to save cost without big quality loss.

[05:42] Lena: what's the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted? latency SLOs?
[05:45] Sara: Hosted is best-effort with transparent perf profiles; Dedicated has reserved capacity with SLA-backed throughput and latency tiers. Private depends on your infra but we provide tooling to monitor and set SLOs.

[06:00] Ravi: real question — can you run our benchmarks? we have two workloads: a) conversational support threads ~8k tokens, b) contract ingestion ~20k tokens. we'd want to measure end-to-end latency and token cost.
[06:10] Miguel: yes, we can do a benchmark. we'd need sample payloads and an agreed test harness — we can run against hosted model variants and a small dedicated test pool or a private eval.
[06:20] Tom: data sharing — is it safe to share sanitized samples?
[06:24] Dana: we can produce sanitized corpora, but need a DPA and NDA in place.
[06:29] Sara: we can send our standard NDA/DPA; for the benchmark we can accept sanitized samples and we will delete them after testing per your retention policy.

[06:40] Miguel: a couple technical notes — long context implies larger KV caches and memory pressure; for 20k contexts we often recommend A100/Tr4 class GPUs and specific kernel paths. quantization can help, but for highest accuracy you might keep fp16.
[06:55] Ravi: do you have recommended GPU sizing for Dedicated?
[06:58] Miguel: yes, we'll send a sizing guide but rough ballpark: 1-2x A100-80GB equivalents per high-concurrency shard for 20k contexts, smaller for 8k. Redwood's autoscaling supports burst to handle spikes.

[07:10] Lena: what about multilang fine-tuning? we have labeled support intents in multiple languages. do you help with finetuning or instruction tuning?
[07:18] Sara: Redwood's research/applied ML team helps with model onboarding and fine-tuning for customers on Dedicated/Private tiers. For Hosted we provide curated models and can do managed fine-tunes as an add-on.

[07:30] Ravi: any gotchas around function calling with quantized models?
[07:33] Miguel: yes — some quantization profiles degrade generation of exact JSON-like structured output. we recommend running a small eval set to validate function-call reliability when using int8 or other aggressive quant. Redwood Optimize flags risky profiles.

[07:48] Tom: competitors — we've been talking to OpenAI and Anthropic; why Redwood?
[07:53] Sara: quick — we focus on production inference economics and consistent tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. you get observability (token-level cost/latency), rollouts, and fallback policies that keep apps online under load. also our model catalog helps with curated open-model tradeoffs.
[08:07] Lena: pricing openness? can you share ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:12] Sara: yes, we'll send a Dedicated pricing sheet and Hosted per-token comparisons. Dedicated tends to be commit-based monthly with lower unit cost for volume.

[08:21] Dana: one more on security — does Redwood provide per-route RBAC and auditability for model access? we need to ensure only certain teams can call private models.
[08:29] Miguel: yes, RBAC is supported and audit logs can be exported to customer SIEMs.

[08:35] Ravi: are there latency numbers we can expect for 8k vs 20k on a Dedicated A100 node? ballpark p99?
[08:42] Miguel: ballpark: for optimized kernels on A100, 8k conversational could be in the 200-400ms per-token regime depending on batch size; 20k can be 2x-4x that per-request in some cases. exacts depend on prompt composition and generation length.

[09:00] Tom: that per-token number seems high compared to OpenAI — are we comparing right?
[09:04] Miguel: differences are often due to optimized batching, model architecture, and sequence length. OpenAI manages a lot of engineering at scale; with Dedicated you get predictability and lower unit cost at commit but may need to tune to hit exact latency targets.

[09:18] Lena: okay — let's talk practical next steps and signal. we have a procurement cycle that triggers enterprise DPA and a pilot with a 3-month evaluation for infrastructure. timeline aim is pilot start by end of january.
[09:30] Sara: sounds reasonable. proposed next steps below.

[09:35] [Recap and next steps]
[09:36] Sara: 1) we'll send Dedicated pricing and SOC2 + compliance pack 2) miguel will own an intake for benchmark — we need sanitized samples and test harness 3) schedule a technical deep dive for infra/security with your ops team next week 4) draft pilot SOW for a 3-month evaluation.
[09:55] Lena: yes please, also include a sample sizing guide and example SLA language.
[09:58] Dana: we'll expect DPA/NDA before sharing samples.

[10:05] Miguel: i'll follow up with a benchmark template and suggested metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens, accuracy on your eval set, tool-call success rate).
[10:15] Ravi: perfect. also can you include a note on function-calling reliability with quantized checkpoints?
[10:20] Miguel: yes i'll add that to the benchmark doc.

[10:26] Tom: any docs you can share right now? decks, benchmark spreadsheets?
[10:29] Sara: i'll drop links — Redwood hosted catalog, dedicated pricing pdf, SOC2 pack, and a benchmark spreadsheet.
[10:36] Lena: ok thanks.

[10:40] Sara: anything else?
[10:42] Dana: just to reiterate, encryption and retention controls are musts.
[10:46] Sara: understood. we'll make those explicit in the SOW.

[10:50] Sara: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of day tomorrow with docs and a proposed time for the deep-dive.
[10:58] Lena: thanks.
[11:00] End of call.
